audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart said Skill at Level 1, Tryndamere at Level 3, Skill at 4-5 and Skill at 6, contradicting both the packet chart and the whys[] text on the same page.
audit.why: packet.levelChart reads Tryndamere/Tryndamere/Aatrox/Aatrox/Tryndamere/Tryndamere/Tryndamere and the mirror audit agrees: Level 1 Tryndamere, Levels 3 and 4-5 Aatrox, Level 6 Tryndamere.
audit.corrected: Level 1 Tryndamere, Level 3 Aatrox, Levels 4-5 Aatrox, Level 6 Tryndamere; both layers proposed as pairs.

audit.whatIsWrong: Undying Rage's 5-second duration and 120/100/80s cooldown, and World Ender's 120/100/80s cooldown, were never stated where the spike advice is given.
audit.why: Both ultimates share the same base cooldown, so the level-6 spike is a race for who spends first; the numbers make the advice actionable.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text now states the 5s window and the 120s World Ender cooldown to fight on.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never named Deathbringer Stance, The Darkin Blade, Infernal Chains or Umbral Dash, and never mentioned that Aatrox's sustain comes off his passive and E.
audit.why: Deathbringer Stance heals on max-health-based bonus damage and Umbral Dash heals on champion damage; World Ender increases that healing. Grievous Wounds timing is the decisive interaction. Infernal Chains drags you back to the centre unless you leave the zone.
audit.corrected: spikes[0].text names The Darkin Blade, Umbral Dash, Deathbringer Stance and Infernal Chains' drag-back; dosFull[0].d and dontsFull[1].d carry the anti-heal and World Ender cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Deathbringer Stance is an auto-attack reset, so his burst opens on an auto wind-up rather than a spell cast.
audit.why: The tell for stepping out is the empowered auto animation, not the Q cast.
audit.corrected: Recorded here; not written to prose this pass because no writable field had room without dropping a live interaction.

edits.before: This is Aatrox's window: once he has Q1-Q2-Q3 plus E dash, he can chain sweet-spots and heal off his W-chained damage while your Q Bloodlust heals stay small. Sidestep the third Q's slam edge and don't trade into a full combo.
edits.after: This is Aatrox's window: The Darkin Blade's three swings plus Umbral Dash let him sweet-spot you while Deathbringer Stance heals off your health bar. Sidestep each slam edge, and leave Infernal Chains' circle before it drags you back in.

edits.before: Your R Undying Rage flips the fight. Aatrox's whole kill pattern relies on executing you low, but if you pop Undying Rage you survive his combo, top your Fury bar off crits, and Q-heal back to full while his W and E are down.
edits.after: Undying Rage flips the fight: five seconds of unkillable beats his execute pattern, and you top your Fury bar off crits then Bloodlust back to full. World Ender is 120s at rank 1 — bait it and fight on its cooldown.

edits.before: His drain spike. Anti-heal and out-crit it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: World Ender is 120s at rank 1 and boosts his healing — engage once it is down or baited.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: His passive and Umbral Dash heal through chip — Executioner's early.

notes: First item row left untouched: packet.levelChart says Tryndamere, the mirror audit says Aatrox. Flagged as a question rather than guessed. dontsFull[1].d was previously unrelated to its own title ('Forget anti-heal'); the replacement fixes that mismatch.
